brief: Morning US Industrials & Materials note with two dedicated previews: airlines and NFP. Airlines: capacity cuts and a better competitive landscape drove RASM growth from flat exiting 2025 to mid-teens in GS's 3Q26 forecast, but jet fuel has risen sharply off its June low to near 2026 highs, so GS cuts 4Q26 industry net income to about $250mm from $3.7bn prior and cuts 2027/2028 net income forecasts 28% and 24%. GS keeps ALGT Buy-rated on a smaller FY26 cut than peers, leading 2027 margins from merger synergies, and a cheap valuation (about 7.5x 2027 earnings vs about 14x historical). NFP: GIR forecasts +80k payrolls, below +88k consensus, as later Labor Day timing drags against low layoffs and a pickup in big-data job indicators, and September will not repeat August's leisure/hospitality and local-education boost; unemployment forecast cut to 4.0% from 4.1% on falling continuing claims; wage growth forecast +0.2% month over month, below consensus, on calendar effects. The desk reflags Q3 longs (ETN, EXPD, PCAR, XPO, TT) against funding shorts (DOV, OC, GWW, AAL, CRH). Macro color: futures up 50bp, France-German spread widening toward 150bp, Brazil's election deadlocked, crude down 3%, the 10-year easing to 5.22%, Bitcoin up 2%.
